title: University of Michigan consumer sentiment — preliminary (Dec 2026), the first prelim whose interviews all post-date the midterms
source: UMICH: TWO of the publisher's own 2026 scheduling documents, both fetched direct and PDF-inflated 2026-11-05 by this event's own initial research (same byte counts the proposing lane recorded the same day). (1) `2026 Release Dates`, data.sca.isr.umich.edu/fetchdoc.php?docid=79628 (HTTP 200, 132,710 bytes), whose text layer reads verbatim "December 4 / December Prelim" between "November 20 / November Final" and "December 18 / December Final", and warns "November and December are a bit off this schedule due to holidays". (2) `2026 Interview Dates`, fetchdoc.php?docid=79629 (HTTP 200, 89,846 bytes), whose December row reads verbatim "November 17 IW Begins / November 30 Prelim Ends / December 14 IW Ends". Promoted estimate -> confirmed and EST: -> UMICH: on the umich-sentiment-prelim-2026-11-06 / -final-2026-11-20 precedents (each promoted off the same two publisher documents in its own initial research). NO CLOCK TIME appears in either document and the apex host sca.isr.umich.edu still does not resolve (curl exit 6, DNS, 2026-11-05), so 10:00 ET is CUSTOMARY, NOT SOURCED; confirmed is a claim about the scheduled date only. Originally proposed 2026-11-05 as proposals/umich-sentiment-prelim-2026-12-04.from-umich-sentiment-prelim-2026-11-06.json, whose finding this canonical file carries forward
notes: Interviews run 2026-11-17 -> 11-30 (published, docid=79629; the normal rule holds: Nov 17 is the Tuesday before the 11-20 final, Nov 30 the Monday before the 12-04 prelim), so EVERY interview post-dates midterm-elections-2026-11-03 by two weeks or more. Strictly, umich-sentiment-final-2026-11-20 is the first RELEASE to carry post-election interviews (its exclusive stretch is 11-03 -> 11-16); this is the first PRELIM whose whole window is post-election. The window CONTAINS retail-sales-2026-11-17, fomc-minutes-2026-11-18, umich-sentiment-final-2026-11-20 (and opex-2026-11-20), pce-2026-11-25 and gdp-q3-2026-second-2026-11-25 (both confirmed, high), Thanksgiving 11-26 and Black Friday 11-27; it contains no CPI (Oct CPI prints 11-10, before it opens; Nov CPI prints mid-December). The release lands on jobs-2026-12-04 at 08:30 ET, so its 10:00 ET tape cannot be attributed to the survey, and five days before fomc-2026-12-09. Impact kept `medium` to match the other 2026 prelims: the prelim surprise gap is structurally live (median |1.75| points vs consensus) even though the print is not tradeable (`symbols: []`, no macro-keyed house playbook). Read-it-do-not-trade-it.
